Ysolde Fenwick.narrative: I was a chapel sister of Brackenford for thirty years, and I left over the gate-due and the silence that let it stand; the sisters heal anyone who comes, I said, so why not the ones the gate calls outlaws? Now I keep a healer's cottage in the old forest, and the sick of every settlement find the path to it, which is more than the gate would allow them. I am sixty-one, my hands are still steady, but the cottage is a long way from a surgeon's hands, and I have a letter under my herb ledger I have not answered. I say what I think about the gate-due to anyone who will listen, and I have never once gone back through that gate.
values: healing without asking who the sick are
the old forest and its gardens kept, not felled
keeping my daughter and grandson close
goals: pay Alder Rush before the first frost without asking the chapel for a mark
keep Orla from the wood road and the pits
decide what to do about Elspeth's letter
keep the salve store full through the winter
learn to set a broken bone cleanly without a surgeon's hands to help
see Hollis read the whole psalter through on his own

relations.name: Orla Fenwick
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Born in this cottage and too ready to walk away from it for a man I do not trust.

relations.name: Hollis Fenwick
relations.label: grandson
relations.note: Knows my herbs better than some sisters I trained; I will not have him afraid of the dark stair or the wood.

relations.name: Sister Elspeth
relations.label: old sister
relations.note: She writes to me still; her letter sits under my ledger and I have not the words for it yet.

relations.name: Alwin Wren
relations.label: old friend
relations.note: He taught me the charms the sisters would not, and he never once told me to go back through the gate.

relations.name: Betony Mossfoot
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: Her salves are honest and her hollow's plants are the same old forest as mine.

relations.name: Marra Brine
relations.label: supplier
relations.note: Roots and barley from the saltings, and a sister's quarrel with Thornby she does not speak of.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: He took my word in the spring; the debt falls due at first frost and I mean to keep my word.

relations.name: Odile Vance
relations.label: old patient's daughter
relations.note: I sat with her mother through her last winter; she sets bones well and has the sense to disapprove of that cairn.

relations.name: Cael Tarn
relations.label: the burner
relations.note: Smoke and drink and a pit house; he is not taking my daughter up that road.

memories.gist: I knelt at the chapel fire and heard the Reeve's men read the Coldwell names as outlaws, and I said nothing, and I have not knelt there since.
Alwin Wren showed me the herb charms the order calls hedge-magic, and I have used them at sickbeds ever since.
I sat three nights with Odile Vance's mother in Kettlebridge and closed her eyes at the end.
Orla was born in this cottage in a hard frost, and I cut the cord myself and thought I would never be so afraid again.
Elspeth's letter came up the forest path in spring, and I read it twice and put it under the herb ledger.

stances.why: I left the order over it; a healer who asks first what a body has done is no healer.
It is taken from folk who never chose the Reeve, and the chapel kept silent about it.
The old forest is the garden and the medicine both; fallen wood serves.
A healer's credit is all she has when the salves run out.
I have seen what a pit house and a drinking man leave a woman with.

Ysolde Fenwick.secret: Elspeth has written asking me back to the chapel before winter, with a pardon for leaving offered through the Reeve; I have told no one, and the letter lies under my herb ledger.
pastimes: walking the old forest paths to see which herbs have come up
sitting with a patient through the evening, telling old chapel stories to settle them
keeping a small garden of the plants she will not trust to the wood
Ysolde Fenwick.calling: I heal whoever finds the path to my door, and I ask nothing at the gate.

Orla Fenwick.narrative: I was born in this cottage and I will likely die in it, but not before I have seen a little of the wood road. I keep the clearing's roots and barley and the beehives, and carry the surplus down to Ferncross and the Fernhollow stall, and that is how I came to know the Sootwood pits and Cael's nephew. My mother has forbidden him the cottage path; I go anyway when the loads are carried, and I am not a girl to be told who may walk up to my own door. The hives have been poor this year and I am short on what I promised Alder, and I have not told her how short.
values: my own choosing, right or wrong
the clearing fed and the honey sold
keeping faith with those who deal fair with me
goals: settle Alder Rush's honey before the frost
keep walking to the pits whatever my mother says
get a better year from the hives
see that Hollis is not afraid of the wood
raise a swarm of her own from the old hive
see the Sootwood pits and the burners' fires with her own eyes, not just the road to them
Orla Fenwick.mood: restless, fond, and quietly anxious about the honey

relations.name: Ysolde Fenwick
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She healed half the island and cannot bear that I choose a man she has not chosen.

relations.name: Hollis Fenwick
relations.label: son
relations.note: He stacks kindling better than the burner taught him, and he is the reason I keep the clearing.

relations.name: Cael Tarn
relations.label: the burner
relations.note: His nephew is kind and patient with Hollis; the rest is my mother's old quarrel with smoke.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: I promised him last autumn's honey and the hives failed me; I will not be a cheat.

relations.name: Rill Fenlake
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She punts the lake and trades fair, and she does not lecture me about the road.

relations.name: Vetch Quill
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: We trade honey and barley, and we both know what a poor year the hives have had.

relations.name: Betony Mossfoot
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: Her salves go down the east road with my honey, and she never asks about the pits.

relations.name: Pell Tarn
relations.label: the burner's kin
relations.note: A boy who wants the quay boats; his cousin is the one I walk to see.

memories.gist: I carried the first full pack of honey down to the Fernhollow stall and sold every pot before noon.
Hollis was born in the cottage with my mother's hands on me, and the wolves were howling close that night.
I met Cael's nephew at the Sootwood pits when I carried honey up the wood road, and he showed me how the slow pits are stacked.
My mother forbade him the cottage path, and I took the next load up the road anyway.
The hives came out poor this summer, and I counted the pots twice and knew I was short of what I promised Alder.

stances.why: I am thirty-four and I have kept this clearing since I was a girl; I will not be told who may come up the path.
A cheat's honey does not sell twice at the Fernhollow stall.
My mother's grudge against the smoke is an old woman's quarrel; the burners have been kind to Hollis.
He is nine and the forest is his home; I will not have him frightened of his own clearing.
Ferncross and Fernhollow are the only markets that do not ask me to kneel to a gate.

Orla Fenwick.secret: I am far shorter on the honey than I have told my mother, and I am thinking of selling my grandmother's silver spoon, the last thing of my father's house, to pay Alder Rush.
pastimes: tending the beehives and watching the bees at the garden edge
walking the loads down the wood road to Ferncross and the Fernhollow stall
sitting with Rill Fenlake over a cup when the carrying is done
Orla Fenwick.calling: I keep the clearing's roots and barley and honey, and I would keep more of it if the bees would let me.

Hollis Fenwick.narrative: I live in the cottage in the clearing with my mother and my grandmother, and I know every path of it and the names of all the herbs in the garden. Grandmother is teaching me my letters from the chapel psalter, and I carry her salve packets down to the Ferncross market in a basket. I like it when Fennel and Bracken come up the path from Fernhollow, and I like the burner who taught me to stack kindling, though Grandmother's face closes when his name is said.
values: the herbs and the salve packets
goals: learn all the herb names in the garden
read the whole psalter without help
play with Fennel and Bracken when they come up the path
learn the name of every plant in the garden and the wood besides

relations.name: Ysolde Fenwick
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: She knows every herb and every charm, and her hands are warm when she sets a poultice.

relations.name: Orla Fenwick
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She carries the honey down the road and always comes back before dark.

relations.name: Fennel Underbank
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He comes up the path from Fernhollow and we hunt for beetles in the woodpile.

relations.name: Bracken Rush
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He counts the packs and lets me count them too.

relations.name: Cael Tarn
relations.label: the burner
relations.note: He taught me to stack kindling so the pit draws, and he does not laugh when I ask questions.

memories.gist: Grandmother set me to name the herbs in the garden and I got eleven right before I forgot the feverfew.
I carried the salve packets down to the Ferncross market in my own basket for the first time.
The burner showed me how to stack the kindling in a cone so the slow pit draws.

pastimes: hunting the garden for every herb and naming it aloud
playing with Fennel and Bracken when they come up the path
stacking kindling the way the burner showed him
Hollis Fenwick.calling: I want to learn my letters and the herbs, and one day carry more than salve packets.
